style: Tactile macro photography of hand-knapped obsidian living seed guardians, with sharply concave conchoidal fracture scars and scalloped pressure-flaked edges.
direction: Jared22Nov: keep the approved unusual art styles and bridge them into something tangible.

artworks.prompt: Create one original Glaze SPALLWORK SANCTUARY artwork called HOLLOW-HORN STAG. A tangible invented forest guardian, unmistakably a standing stag with a long alert head, four slender articulated legs and huge asymmetrical branching horns, but constructed as a living knapped-obsidian sculpture. This is not a normal black deer: its rib-body is a broad open vaulted chamber with three little seed cradles sheltered inside, and its horns branch into broad thin forked stone lamellae with an open crooked arch. Material is black volcanic glass shaped by traditional percussion flaking: every surface has large sharply defined CONCAVE conchoidal flake scars, scalloped pressure-flaked edges, intersecting opaque charcoal planes and tiny grey-silver rim highlights. Strictly no liquid-smooth surfaces, rectangular hopper crystals, iridescent rainbow metal, polished gemstone or plastic. High-end tactile studio macro photography of a real knapped miniature, pale warm light raking across chipped concavities, strong black silhouette with readable subtle internal texture. Three-quarter view facing left; whole head, antlers, four feet and tail in frame. Central 78 percent of a SQUARE canvas, generous genuinely transparent alpha around and through every gap. No ground, pedestal, cast background shadow, text, logo, frame or collage. Intriguing calm crafted guardian with a purposeful seed-keeping anatomy, not horror, skeleton or cute cartoon. Visibly separate material from glossy magnetic fluid, porous foam, inflated latex or bismuth terraces.
artworks.export: Original retained; selected artwork fitted whole within 960px on a 1024px transparent square. Wallpaper unchanged.
